title: Unable to build testbench waveform in ubuntu
body:
Tried building the testbench.vcd in ubuntu 12.04 with vivado,

getting error as below.

prashantravi@ubuntu:~/picorv32/picorv32$ make testbench.vcd 
iverilog -o testbench.exe testbench.v picorv32.v
picorv32.v:41: syntax error
I give up.
make: **\* [testbench.exe] Error 2
prashantravi@ubuntu:~/picorv32/picorv32$ 

Please help

comments.body:
I think you have modified the picorv32 makefile, it should look like this:

```
testbench.vcd: testbench.exe firmware/firmware.hex
    vvp -N $< +vcd
```

I assume you changed it because you don't have the riscv toolchain on your path. if you install the toolchain like is described in the README file, and make testbench.vcd should work just fine.
Undo your changes to your git branch with `git reset --hard && git checkout origin/master`.

@prashantrar: It seems you have an older version of Icarus Verilog. Quoting the PicoRV32 README.md file:

> Note: The test bench is using Icarus Verilog. However, Icarus Verilog 0.9.7 (the latest release at the time of writing) has a few bugs that prevent the test bench from running. Upgrade to the latest github master of Icarus Verilog to run the test bench.

I think the recently released Icarus Verilog 10.0 should also work..

@dvc94ch: It's already the rule for testbench.exe that fails:

```
testbench.exe: testbench.v picorv32.v
        iverilog -o testbench.exe testbench.v picorv32.v
        chmod -x testbench.exe
```
@cliffordwolf Thanks, the answer helped. it is working for me now. Just needed to download latest version of icarus verilog.

title: Current riscv gnu toolchain failed on Ubuntu 16.0 due to lacking expat
body:
```
checking whether to use expat... yes
checking for libexpat... no
configure: error: expat is missing or unusable
Makefile:9095: recipe for target 'configure-gdb' failed
make[2]: *** [configure-gdb] Error 1
make[2]: Leaving directory '/home/ubuntu/projects/picorv32/riscv-gnu-toolchain-rv32i/build/build-gdb-newlib'
Makefile:848: recipe for target 'all' failed
make[1]: *** [all] Error 2
make[1]: Leaving directory '/home/ubuntu/projects/picorv32/riscv-gnu-toolchain-rv32i/build/build-gdb-newlib'
Makefile:394: recipe for target 'stamps/build-gdb-newlib' failed
make: *** [stamps/build-gdb-newlib] Error 2
```

This seems to be a recently added dependency, because I've successfully build earlier toolchains on the same machine in the past.

Fix: installed `expat` and `libexpt1-dev`. Not sure if you need to install both of them or if the failure is somehow specific to my Ubuntu installation (which is running on a Vagrant VM.)

fix_commits.messageHeadline: Add libexpt1-dev to list of Ubuntu packages needed for building tools…

comments.body: Same problem with Ubuntu 18.04, fixed by installing `libexpt1-dev`.

title: Bug: global variable declaration and init not possible in one step
body:
During https://github.com/cliffordwolf/picorv32/issues/92 I found that I cannot declare and initialize variables at the same time, like

> int firstSensor = 1;    // first analog sensor
int secondSensor = 2;   // second analog sensor
int thirdSensor = 3;    // digital sensor
int inByte = 0;         // incoming serial byte

it will produce code that does not work. E.g. 2 LEDs being ON even though this never happens in the code used.

In order to make it work I have to split declaration and init like:

> int firstSensor;    // first analog sensor
int secondSensor;   // second analog sensor
int thirdSensor;    // digital sensor
int inByte;         // incoming serial byte
void main()
{
	firstSensor = 1;    // first analog sensor - dummy value
	secondSensor = 2;   // second analog sensor - dummy value
	thirdSensor = 3;    // digital sensor - dummy value
	inByte = 0;         // incoming serial byte
...

fix_commits.messageHeadline: Alignment fix for global symbols fixes #97

comments.body: Which linker script are you using? What `start.s`? Obviously you are not handling the `data`/`sdata` section correctly. But it's impossible to reproduce the issue from the little information you posted. Please post a [MCVE](https://stackoverflow.com/help/mcve).
It's based on https://github.com/FPGAwars/Alhambra-II-FPGA/tree/master/examples/picorv32/picosoc so the same `start.s` as in there. As soon as I have time I will build a MCVE for you.

Use the repo mentioned before and following minimal example (on Alhambra 2 board):
[firmware.c](https://github.com/cliffordwolf/picorv32/files/2521969/firmware.c.txt)

The LED bar should fill up and then all LEDs should flash all at the same time. But instead only 2 LEDs turn on even though this never happens in the code used. It seems to be related to the print statement too. Hope this is now a valid MCVE. Greetings.
@drtrigon if you could please try to apply latest change to .ld file and confirm if it works on your environment ? Thanks
Works in the test case for me. Also did another test in the originating code were the issue first appeared and this worked too - looks like a good fix to me. Thanks!
